body:
I don't think any required check actually runs this case yet (or the packer section, or the new `t_amx_dispatch_dtype` expectations). GCP Nix builds through `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix`, which sets neither `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` nor `TRON_K_VNNI`. With dispatch off, `amx_attn.cpp` isn't added to `tron` (`src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:219-224`) and both AMX binaries compile only their `SUCCEED("... nothing to test")` stub. So the `passed t_amx_numerics 0.5s` on this head's Test host has to be that stub. (I'm going by the build config here: Slice only uploads per-test output on failure.) The only lane with both options (`cmake-single-platform.yml`) is dispatch/call-only and hasn't run on this branch.

AGENTS.md says a committed test has to execute in a required suite unless the user explicitly approves an exception. #4865 states that approval, but the issue has no comments and this PR has no reviews yet. Could we either add the two options to the Nix test build, or get the exception recorded on this PR? Adding the options would get the fake-based dispatch test and the packer section running on every PR, since neither needs AMX. In the meantime, a manual `gh workflow run cmake-single-platform.yml --ref jhan-vnnik-2-amx` with the run id in the description would at least show the option-on build compiles.

_How I checked: `grep -rn 'TRON_AMX_DISPATCH\|TRON_K_VNNI' nix/ flake.nix .github/workflows/` only hits `cmake-single-platform.yml:355-356`, and both options default OFF (`CMakeLists.txt:46-47`). The stubs are at `t_amx_numerics.cpp:367-373` and `t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:306-310`. The packer TEST_CASE (:119) has no `available()` guard. `gh run list --commit 26b86a2` shows only GCP Nix and Debian smoke, and the legacy workflow has no runs for `jhan-vnnik-2-amx`. The Test host log (job 117146725032) shows both AMX binaries passing in 0.5 s. `gh issue view 4865 --json comments` has 0 comments, and `gh api .../pulls/4957/reviews` has none besides mine._

Even once an option-on build runs this, I think a green result won't tell us whether the kernel ran. The host-test jobs ask for `[self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]`, and that matches the three Genoa andoria runners as well as the three Granite Rapids delphi ones. On Genoa this WARNs, returns, and reports as passed. This head's Test host did land on `andoria-14-0`.

Two small ideas: use Catch2 `SKIP(...)` here so a non-AMX landing shows up as a skip (the repo already maps all-skipped binaries through `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 4`, `t/CMakeLists.txt:354-362`), and give one job an `intel` label (or an env var like `TRON_REQUIRE_AMX=1` that turns this into a `FAIL`) so at least one run per PR executes it for real. The same guard sits on the older QK and PV cases at :173 and :282, so this would cover them too.

_How I checked: the guards are at `t_amx_numerics.cpp:173, :232, :282`; the runner table at `README.ci.md:447-452` (andoria = Genoa, delphi = Granite Rapids, all six carry `fpga test avx512`); `gh api .../runs/38948262312/jobs` shows Test host on `andoria-14-0` and Test FPGA on `delphi-17cf-0`, and Test FPGA's 58 tests don't include `t_amx_numerics` (it's registered `LABELS fake`, `t/CMakeLists.txt:618`)._

Small one, and probably more the parent PR's concern than this one's: once the stack lands, I don't think any lane builds this `else` arm (or the row-major packer arm at :1702) with AMX dispatch on. #4956 moved the legacy lane to `-DTRON_K_VNNI=ON`, so the only option-on build now takes the VNNI arm. Meanwhile the `deb` preset ships `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON` with VNNI off, which is exactly this arm. Both `else` arms are the exact calls from before this PR, so it's low risk today. Still, a future edit here would ship in the package with no test reaching it. A second option-on leg with VNNI off would cover it, or at least a line in README.ci.md saying that only the `deb` build covers this arm.

_How I checked: `git show origin/main:.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml` has `-DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON` alone at :355, while the base `a5697f86d3` adds `-DTRON_K_VNNI=ON` at :356; `CMakePresets.json` `deb` sets `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH: ON` and `ENABLE_TESTS: OFF` with no `TRON_K_VNNI`; no other workflow or Nix file sets either option; `git diff a5697f86d3...26b86a279a -- h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp` shows the old `pack_q_group_128x4`/`qk_rowmajor_128x4` calls moved into the `else` arms unchanged._

K got a typed view here, so a wrong plane can't reach the wrong kernel. Q stops one step short, though. Both packers write `bf16*`, and both QK kernels read `const bf16*`. A group-packed slot handed to `qk_vnni_128x4` (or a rows-packed one handed to `qk_rowmajor_128x4`) compiles cleanly and would score silently wrong. Today the pairing is right because the two `if constexpr` sites in `self_attention.hpp` (:1700 and :1772) test the same constant, and `rows_pack_calls` exists to compensate. Fine as a follow-up: one small `alignas(64)` struct per packing (say `q_rows_pack` / `q_group_pack`), `amx_qpack_slot` picked with `std::conditional_t` on `layout_on`, and two `STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE` cross-probes next to the new ones in `t_llama_unit`. Then the swap becomes a compile error and the counter can go.

_How I checked: a syntax-only probe that feeds `pack_q_group_128x4`'s output to `qk_vnni_128x4` compiles with exit 0 (`clang++` 19 from the Nix store, `-std=c++23 -fsyntax-only` against this head's `h/`); the declarations at iface:191, :236, :244 and :253 all take plain `bf16` pointers; `amx_qpack_slot` (`self_attention.hpp:260`) is one type for both packers; the comment at `t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:60` notes the shared signature._

This fake ignores its K view and its Q pointer, and the test never looks at the attention result. So if `apply_dense_amx_page` handed the kernel a stale or wrong `q_packed` slot, or another (slot, kv_head)'s plane, the test would still pass. The row-major fake already had this shape, so it isn't new. But as far as I can tell this is the only test of the dispatch wiring that runs without AMX hardware, so it seems worth closing. A cheap option: have the packer fakes record their `output` pointer and the QK fakes record the `q` pointer they got, then `REQUIRE` the two match (and maybe that the K view's plane is the one for the slot and head under test).

_How I checked: read the fakes at :249-270 (unnamed K/Q parameters, zero-filled output), and `rg -n 'REQUIRE|CHECK' t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp` lists only call counts, visit tallies and `probe.q`. The numerical page test at `t_llama_unit.cpp:2490-2520` uses float and 2 query heads per KV head, so it never reaches this path either._

Small idea: `s_vnni` is exactly 4 rows, so if the copy-out loop ever regressed to 16 rows, the kernel would write 3 KiB past this buffer onto the stack. Whether the test then fails would depend on frame layout, not on the bug. The production caller's `s_pages` is also exactly 4 rows (`self_attention.hpp:1767-1771`), so "s needs only 4 rows" is a real contract worth pinning. Could we declare this one `[TILE_ROWS_16][PAGE_TOKENS_64]`, keep the 0xff fill, and `REQUIRE` rows 4..15 are still all-0xff afterwards, like the packer section's poison check?

_How I checked: `s_vnni` at :258 is `[GROUP_HEADS_4][PAGE_TOKENS_64]`; the 4-row contract rests only on the loop bound `r < GROUP_HEADS_4` at `amx_attn.cpp:287`, while `s16` itself holds 16 rows._

Tiny latent one: this always copies 64 floats per row, so the contract "s[4][s_stride_floats]" (iface:248) quietly assumes `s_stride_floats >= 64`. A caller that takes the comment literally and passes a smaller stride would overlap rows and run off the end. Every caller passes 64 today, and `qk_rowmajor_128x4` has the same gap, so this is just about making the precondition visible: either `TRON_ASSERT_LE(PAGE_TOKENS_64, s_stride_floats);` at the top of both kernels (`h/common/assert.hpp` isn't included in this TU yet), or a "`s_stride_floats >= PAGE_TOKENS_64`" in the declaration comment.

_How I checked: the row-major kernel likewise stores 16 floats at `s + k * s_stride_floats + r * 16` for r = 0..3 (`amx_attn.cpp:215-219`), so 64 per row whatever the stride; every call site (`self_attention.hpp:1773/1776`, `t_amx_numerics.cpp:187/261/264`) passes `page::page_size`/`PAGE_TOKENS_64`; `amx_attn.cpp` has no `TRON_ASSERT` at all._

A question for later, not a blocker. With Q as the A operand, 12 of the 16 rows of this tile and of the four accumulators are zeros, because `begin_region` configures every tile at 16 rows. That setting made sense when K was A. As far as I know, palette 1 allows a 4-row A and C with 16-row B tiles (TDPBF16PS needs C.rows = A.rows and A.colsb/4 = B.rows, and 64/4 = 16 here). With that config this could load straight from `q.data` and `_tile_stored` straight into `s` with the caller's stride. Then `pack_q_rows_128x4`, the padding contract, `s16` and the row copy would all go away, and the PV kernel's `P`/`o` would shrink the same way. I'm honestly not sure TDPBF16PS cost scales with the configured row count, so it's probably worth one A/B on a Granite Rapids box before PRs 3 and 4 build on this shape. One wrinkle: the identity case runs both kernels inside a single `begin_region`, so it would need a region per kernel.

_How I checked: `amx_attn.cpp:121-129` sets all 8 tiles to `TILE_ROWS_16`. `pack_q_rows_128x4` copies 1 KiB into a 4 KiB slot (:224-228). The kernel stores 4 KiB into `s16` and copies 1 KiB out (:283-289). The PV kernel's `P` is a 16-row tile with rows 4..15 zero, and `o` holds 16 rows (:301-306). The tile-shape rule is from my reading of the ISA and is not checked here, and nothing is measured; I don't have an AMX host._

Nit: as far as I know, `TILELOADD`/`TILESTORED` take any base address and stride and have no alignment requirement. A misaligned plane would still load correctly, just with split lines. So for the tiles, 64-byte alignment is a performance and design invariant rather than a need. The static check is worth keeping either way. Maybe:

```suggestion
  // The 64-byte pair rows need a 64-byte-aligned plane; the AMX tile loads
  // then read whole cache lines.
```

(Same wording question for the V-plane line at :433, which came from the base PR.)

_How I checked: this is from my understanding of the SDM's TILELOADD/TILESTORED semantics, not something I re-read or ran for this review (no AMX host here). A load from a deliberately misaligned buffer would settle it, so happy to be corrected._

body:
This is accurate as written, but read next to "so CI covers that code" a few lines up (:584), I think it suggests the identity case runs in PR CI. Today no PR-triggered build sets `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` (#4865). The only lane that does is the legacy one, which runs on `workflow_dispatch` or from `publish-deb.yml` for tags and feature branches. Could we say that here, e.g.:

```suggestion
exercises the store and the AMX kernel `qk_vnni_128x4`. That case compiles in
every `TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON` build, with or without this option, and executes
AMX only on a Granite Rapids runner, as above. No pull-request build sets
`TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` yet (issue #4865), so today only the legacy CMake lane,
run by hand or from `publish-deb.yml`, compiles it. The
```

_How I checked: `cmake-single-platform.yml:5-14` triggers only on `workflow_dispatch`/`workflow_call`; `publish-deb.yml:64-68` calls it only for tags or feature-branch publishes; no file under `nix/` or `.github/workflows/` other than that lane sets either option._
